newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Landslide hits Australian ski resort, many trapped.
newsitem.headline: Landslide hits Australian ski resort, many trapped.

text.p: Up to 20 people were feared missing and many more injured when a landslide demolished two lodges at Australia's busiest ski resort, police and rescue officials said on Thursday.

Police said rescuers working in sub-zero temperatures were unable to begin searching the wreckage at the Thredbo Alpine Village, in the Snowy Mountains about 150 km (90 miles) southwest of Canberra, because the site remained dangerously unstable.
"(There are) early suggestions that we have about 18-20 people that have not been accounted for," a police spokesman said from Sydney.
"The site instability is hampering the rescue operation ... it's very unstable unfortunately."
Local police said it appeared several dozen people had been injured but the exact number and the extent of their injuries was not known.
There were early media reports that some people had been killed. Police could not confirm this, although one senior officer said it was almost certain that people had died.

"At this point in time it is my belief that it's highly likely that we will have a number of fatalities," Superintendent Charlie Sanderson told reporters in the mountain town of Jindabyne, about 35 km (20 miles) from the scene of the disaster.
He said snow expected in the area on Thursday could further hamper rescue operations. There was little snow on the ground at the time of the landslide, but road conditions in the area were icy.
The landslide occurred just before midnight on Wednesday at a time when Thredbo is packed with thousands of visitors at the height of Australia's skiing season.
Police set up roadblocks at Jindabyne to block access to the resort.
Engineers, geologists and mine rescue experts were being brought in to assess the situation.
Witnesses said the scene was a jumble of debris and wreckage.

"The word is that it is too unstable at this point. There is too much debris, including concrete slabs, trees, automobiles ... timber on the site," said one witness quoted by Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.
"It's quite a steep slope and it's just too unstable to go in, to risk any more lives at this stage. They have not given us the okay to go in and start searching," he said.
Rescuers and ambulances, including air ambulances, were rushing to the scene from as far away as Sydney, a five to six hour drive in normal conditions.
Rescue officials said they were unable to get helicopters into the area because of the icy conditions.
